title: Boss: the merge gatekeeper
summary: Build the checks that decide whether a pull request may merge.

steps.title: The gatekeeper
steps.body: Your team wants one service that reads the CI results for a pull request and says yes or no, with reasons a developer can act on.

steps.title: Gate with reasons
prompt: Write `List<string> GateFailures(int failedTests, double coverage, double minCoverage, int criticalVulns)`. Return, in this order, only the rules that fail:
- `"coverage 72.5% below 80.0%"` when coverage < minimum (both with one decimal, `F1`)
An empty list means the gate passes.
starter: List<string> GateFailures(int failedTests, double coverage, double minCoverage, int criticalVulns)
solution: List<string> GateFailures(int failedTests, double coverage, double minCoverage, int criticalVulns)
hints: Three independent `if`s, each adding a message.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("all good", new List<string>(), GateFailures(0, 85, 80, 0));
Dojo.Eq("everything wrong", new List<string> { "tests failed: 3", "coverage 72.5% below 80.0%", "critical vulnerabilities: 2" }, GateFailures(3, 72.5, 80, 2));
Dojo.Eq("exactly at the floor passes", new List<string>(), GateFailures(0, 80, 80, 0));
Dojo.Eq("only coverage", new List<string> { "coverage 79.9% below 80.0%" }, GateFailures(0, 79.9, 80, 0));

steps.title: Retries, visibly
prompt: A test may be retried up to `maxRetries` times (so at most `1 + maxRetries` attempts count). `attempts` lists the results in order (`true` = pass);
ignore attempts beyond the limit. Write `string Outcome(List<bool> attempts, int maxRetries)`:
- `"flaky-pass"` when a later counted attempt passed
hints: `Take(1 + maxRetries)` keeps only the attempts that count.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("green first time", "pass", Outcome(new() { true }, 2));
Dojo.Eq("passed on retry", "flaky-pass", Outcome(new() { false, false, true }, 2));
Dojo.Eq("pass came too late", "fail", Outcome(new() { false, false, true }, 1));
Dojo.Eq("no retries allowed", "fail", Outcome(new() { false, true }, 0));
Dojo.Eq("never ran", "fail", Outcome(new(), 3));

steps.title: Coverage ratchet
prompt: A **ratchet** lets coverage go up but never fall by more than a tolerance. Write
`double? Ratchet(double baseline, double current, double tolerance)`:
- if `current < baseline - tolerance`, return `null` (the gate fails)
- otherwise return the new baseline: the larger of `baseline` and `current`
starter: double? Ratchet(double baseline, double current, double tolerance)
solution: double? Ratchet(double baseline, double current, double tolerance)
hints: Returning `null` from a `double?` method is allowed.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("coverage went up", (double?)84.0, Ratchet(80, 84, 0.5));
Dojo.Eq("small dip is tolerated, baseline kept", (double?)80.0, Ratchet(80, 79.6, 0.5));
Dojo.Check("big drop fails", Ratchet(80, 78, 0.5) == null, "expected null");

steps.title: Shard the suite
prompt: To finish faster, CI splits tests across `shards` parallel jobs. Write `List<string> Shard(List<(string Test, int Ms)> tests, int shards)`:
1. Take tests from longest to shortest (ties: by name, ordinal).
2. Give each one to the shard with the **smallest total time so far** (ties: the lowest shard index).
3. Return one string per shard: its test names joined by `,` in the order they were assigned (empty string for an empty shard).
starter: List<string> Shard(List<(string Test, int Ms)> tests, int shards)
solution: List<string> Shard(List<(string Test, int Ms)> tests, int shards)
var names = Enumerable.Range(0, shards).Select(_ => new List<string>()).ToList();
foreach (var (test, ms) in tests.OrderByDescending(t => t.Ms).ThenBy(t => t.Test, StringComparer.Ordinal))
for (int i = 1; i < shards; i++) if (totals[i] < totals[best]) best = i;
hints: Find the shard with the lowest total using a strict `<`, so ties go to the lower index.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("balanced over two shards", new List<string> { "e2e,unitA", "api,db" },
Dojo.Eq("more shards than tests", new List<string> { "a", "b", "" }, Shard(new() { ("a", 5), ("b", 5) }, 3));
Dojo.Eq("one shard keeps everything", new List<string> { "slow,mid,fast" }, Shard(new() { ("fast", 1), ("slow", 9), ("mid", 5) }, 1));
